about.title: About Grantora
about.lead: Grantora is a platform that helps students find scholarships, grants and international programmes worldwide, prepare for them and track deadlines.
about.whatP: A catalogue and a personal dashboard in one place: you search and save grants, prepare documents and follow application stages. The platform works in Uzbek, Russian and English.
about.missionP: To make international education opportunities open, understandable and trustworthy for everyone.
about.help1: Quickly find a suitable grant with filters.
about.help3: Application stages and a document checklist in one place.
about.help4: See how well a grant fits your profile (this is not an admission probability).
about.trustT: How we work with reliable information
about.trustP: Every grant links to an official source. Deadlines go through freshness checks. Sample data are labelled separately. The match percentage is not an admission guarantee.
about.future3: A mobile app and a Telegram bot
about.teamP: Information about the project team will be added soon.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.a1: Grantora brings together scholarships, grants and exchange programmes from around the world for students, and helps you filter them and track deadlines.
faq.a2: Use the catalogue filters for country, study level, type of funding and deadline. After you sign up you also get recommendations that match your profile.
faq.q3: Is applying for a grant free?
faq.a3: Using Grantora is free. Some programmes may charge application or test fees themselves (for example IELTS or document translation): check the terms on the official website.
faq.q4: What is the difference between a full and a partial grant?
faq.a4: A full grant usually covers tuition and basic living costs. A partial grant covers only a part, for example just tuition or a monthly allowance.
faq.a5: Yes, many programmes are open to bachelor's students, while some are only for master's or PhD. Filter by level in the catalogue.
faq.q6: What opportunities exist for a master's degree?
faq.a6: DAAD, Chevening and Fulbright are well-known for master's study. Choose the master's level in the catalogue and narrow it by country and deadline.
faq.q7: Do I have to know English?
faq.a7: IELTS or TOEFL is often required, but some programmes offer a preparatory language year or accept other certificates. Each grant page states its language requirement.
faq.q8: How can I track grant deadlines?
faq.a8: Save a grant or add it to your applications: you get reminders 7, 3 and 1 day before the deadline. You can also export the calendar as an .ics file.
faq.q9: How are documents submitted for a grant?
faq.a9: Documents are submitted on the programme's official website or portal. In Grantora you keep your documents ready and follow them with a checklist.
faq.q10: Can I apply directly through Grantora?
faq.a10: No. Grantora is an information and preparation tool: applications are always submitted through the official website, and the link is on the grant page.
